caption: The drawing consists of a symmetrical floral pattern with stylized flower and leaf motifs, rendered in muted shades of blue-green, mustard yellow, and maroon, all outlined by thin brownish lines. The central object is a large, upright tulip-like flower in the lower half of the image, featuring alternating yellow and maroon sections, with a blue-green stem emerging downward. Above the main flower, three blue-green stems rise vertically, tipped by yellow-and-maroon buds, and are surrounded by clusters of blue-green circular shapes and two maroon, clover-like shapes. Flanking the central flower on each side are identical flower designs, each with six blue-green petals, a yellow center, and maroon core, connected to the main composition by flowing, curved stems. At the bottom left, there is a secondary flower with yellow petals, a maroon base, and a centrally placed yellow circle, as well as a blue-green curling leaf; at bottom right, there is another maroon-and-yellow motif surrounded by several maroon, round-ended shapes and two blue-green leaf-like extensions. The background is a textured, light beige color with a subtle, mottled effect, giving the drawing an aged appearance. At the bottom, there is centered text labeling the design's origin and project affiliation.
title: San Luis Obispo Mission Altar Tabernacle from the portfolio "Decorative Art of Spanish California"
